questions.prompt: Explain the main engineering decision in: Lab: Tensors, autograd & nn.Module
questions.referenceAnswer: Trace the shapes of a batched linear layer. Compare a finite-difference gradient with the gradient computed by autograd.
keyPoints: Trace the shapes of a batched linear layer.
Compare a finite-difference gradient with the gradient computed by autograd.

questions.prompt:
A batch of 16 examples with 8 features passing through a layer with 5 outputs has shape [16, 5]. Treating 16 as the feature count changes the model rather than only its layout.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
A tensor shape is an interface between layers. Write down what each axis means before reshaping: batch, sequence, channel, or feature. A linear layer transforms the last feature axis and keeps preceding axes. Shape-compatible operations can still be semantically wrong when axes are swapped.

The projection changes the final feature dimension and preserves batch and sequence axes.
keyPoints: The projection changes the final feature dimension and preserves batch and sequence axes.
A tensor shape is an interface between layers.

questions.prompt:
Subtracting predictions shaped [32, 1] and targets shaped [32] creates a [32, 32] difference matrix, not 32 independent errors.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Broadcasting compares dimensions from the right. Dimensions are compatible when equal or when one is 1; missing leading dimensions behave as size 1. This can silently create a larger result than intended. Check the resulting shape before interpreting a loss or metric.

Match target and prediction shapes so each prediction is compared with its own target.
keyPoints: Match target and prediction shapes so each prediction is compared with its own target.
Broadcasting compares dimensions from the right.

questions.prompt:
For y = 3x squared, dy/dx = 6x. At x = 2 the derivative is 12; an optimizer still needs to use that derivative to change x.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Autograd records operations performed on tensors that require gradients. Backward applies the chain rule through that graph and accumulates gradients in leaf parameters. The graph reflects the operations actually executed, which makes data-dependent forward paths possible. Gradient recording is different from updating model parameters.

Backward computes gradients; the optimizer update is a separate operation.
keyPoints: Backward computes gradients; the optimizer update is a separate operation.
Autograd records operations performed on tensors that require gradients.

questions.prompt:
Four microbatches intended to form one effective batch should trigger one optimizer step. Clearing gradients after each microbatch discards the earlier contributions.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Gradients accumulate across backward calls. This supports intentional microbatch accumulation but causes errors when accidental. For equal-sized microbatches, dividing each loss by the accumulation count reproduces the gradient of their mean under the same model state. Unequal microbatches require weighting by example count.

Clear once before an accumulation window and step once after its final microbatch.
keyPoints: Clear once before an accumulation window and step once after its final microbatch.
Gradients accumulate across backward calls.

questions.prompt:
A list of hidden layers stored in a plain list may not appear in model.parameters(). A ModuleList registers those layers while allowing a custom forward loop.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
nn.Module tracks assigned parameters and child modules so state dictionaries, optimizers, and device transfers can discover them. Plain Python containers do not register their contents in the same way as ModuleList or ModuleDict. A network can run a forward pass while accidentally omitting parameters from optimization.

Use registered module containers for learnable layers created dynamically.
keyPoints: Use registered module containers for learnable layers created dynamically.
nn.Module tracks assigned parameters and child modules so state dictionaries, optimizers, and device transfers can discover them.

questions.prompt:
With five mutually exclusive classes, each example has five logits and one class index. Five independent binary labels describe a different prediction problem.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Match the model output to the loss definition. Multiclass cross entropy commonly takes raw class logits and class-index targets; applying softmax first is usually the wrong interface. Binary tasks may use a numerically stable logits-based loss. Inspect reduction and masking so the scalar loss represents the intended examples.

Choose the loss from label semantics and its documented input contract.
keyPoints: Choose the loss from label semantics and its documented input contract.
Match the model output to the loss definition.

questions.prompt:
A training loader can shuffle examples and apply random crops. A validation loader should use a reproducible transform so checkpoint comparisons measure model changes rather than random input changes.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
A Dataset maps an index to an example or yields a stream of examples. DataLoader handles batching, workers, and collation. Keep training-only transformations separate from deterministic validation preprocessing. Do not fit normalization or vocabulary statistics on held-out examples just because the loader can access them.

Separate example construction from batching and validation preprocessing.
keyPoints: Separate example construction from batching and validation preprocessing.
A Dataset maps an index to an example or yields a stream of examples.

questions.prompt:
Sequences of lengths 3 and 7 require 14 padded positions in a rectangular batch, but only 10 represent real tokens. Averaging loss over all 14 without masking changes the objective.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Collation combines examples into a batch. Variable-length sequences often require padding plus an attention mask or length vector. Padding values must not contribute incorrectly to a loss or average. Bucketing similar lengths can reduce padding waste but changes batching and shuffling decisions.

Normalize sequence losses over intended valid tokens rather than arbitrary padding positions.
keyPoints: Normalize sequence losses over intended valid tokens rather than arbitrary padding positions.
Collation combines examples into a batch.

questions.prompt:
A GPU may be mostly idle while CPU image decoding saturates one worker. Increasing model batch size alone does not remove that data-loading bottleneck.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
GPU speed depends on keeping the accelerator supplied with data. Data decoding, host memory copies, and synchronization may dominate a small forward pass. Pinned host memory and asynchronous transfer can help in suitable pipelines, but require measurement and correct lifetime handling. Benchmark end-to-end steps rather than isolated kernels only.

Optimize the measured bottleneck in the end-to-end pipeline.
keyPoints: Optimize the measured bottleneck in the end-to-end pipeline.
GPU speed depends on keeping the accelerator supplied with data.

questions.prompt:
A run that becomes faster but produces non-finite gradients is not an improvement. Skipped updates and validation drift belong in the mixed-precision evaluation report.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Autocasting selects lower-precision operations where appropriate while retaining safer precision for sensitive operations. FP16 has limited numerical range; loss scaling can preserve small gradients. BF16 has a wider exponent range but fewer mantissa bits than FP32. Precision changes require quality and stability checks as well as speed measurements.

Evaluate numerical stability and validation behavior alongside mixed-precision speed.
keyPoints: Evaluate numerical stability and validation behavior alongside mixed-precision speed.
Autocasting selects lower-precision operations where appropriate while retaining safer precision for sensitive operations.

questions.prompt:
A weight-only file restores predictions but may not reproduce the next training step. Missing preprocessing can also change inference even when weights load correctly.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
A resumable training checkpoint includes model, optimizer, scheduler, step, data position, and relevant random state. A deployment artifact may need only inference state plus preprocessing metadata. Load artifacts from trusted sources and verify compatibility. Test restoration rather than treating a successful save as evidence of recoverability.

Checkpoint requirements depend on whether the goal is inference or exact training continuation.
keyPoints: Checkpoint requirements depend on whether the goal is inference or exact training continuation.
A resumable training checkpoint includes model, optimizer, scheduler, step, data position, and relevant random state.

questions.prompt:
Four ranks with eight examples each and two accumulation steps yield an effective batch of 64 examples, assuming the losses are weighted consistently.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Distributed data parallel training replicates a model and synchronizes gradients across ranks. Each rank should receive the intended data shard and participate in compatible collective operations. DDP does not automatically reduce per-rank model-state memory. Global batch size combines local batch, accumulation, and participating ranks.

DDP scales work across replicas but generally retains a full model replica per rank.
keyPoints: DDP scales work across replicas but generally retains a full model replica per rank.
Distributed data parallel training replicates a model and synchronizes gradients across ranks.
